topics.label: Lecture introduction and framing
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture topic, contextualizes the difficulty of complement nomenclature, and sets expectations for the session.

topics.label: Foundations and central role of C3 in complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the core biological principles, naming conventions, and the central role of C3 in the complement cascade.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three distinct recognition pathways and mechanisms that drive complement activation and convertase assembly.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the primary downstream effector functions through which activated complement clears pathogens and stimulates inflammation.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement
topics.groupedBecause: It explains the regulatory proteins and mechanisms that prevent complement activation from damaging host tissues.

topics.label: Clinical complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: It outlines the distinct clinical presentations and pathologies resulting from deficiencies in specific complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: It examines the evolutionary strategies and molecular mechanisms used by pathogens, notably Staphylococcus aureus, to evade complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Lecture wrap-up and next session preview
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the complement session and announces the topic of the subsequent lecture.
